results.title: AI Inference Acceleration for Trading with ​Xelera
results.content: # By combining Xelera Silva’s high-performance software with Napatech’s ultra-low latency hardware acceleration, financial institutions gain a market advantage through faster trades, stronger security, and more efficient data processing. ### Xelera Technologies is a software provider for high-speed network technology and machine learning applications. A ready-to-use solution, it eliminates latency bottlenecks and enhances throughput by leveraging Napatech SmartNIC or DPU. The turn-key accelerator connects to the software-based trading system and offloads the AI inference to a Napatech SmartNIC or DPU. The turn-key accelerator connects to the software-based trading system and offloads the XGBoost / LightGBM / CatBoost inference to a Napatech SmartNIC or DPU (ultra-low latency PCIe transfer included in round-trip latency). ## ​Integrating Xelera Silva with Napatech’s SmartNICs and DPUs offers several key benefits for the finance industry, particularly in high-frequency trading (HFT) applications. Napatech’s SmartNICs and DPUs accelerate AI/ML-based fraud detection models, enabling financial institutions to analyze massive datasets without CPU bottlenecks. Napatech SmartNICs and DPUs reduce CPU workloads, lowering data center power consumption and operational costs. ## The Napatech SmartNIC and DPU family for high-performance network acceleration compatible with Xelera Silva. ### The Napatech SmartNIC and DPU family consists of programmable, high-performance Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Data Processing Units (DPUs) designed to accelerate and optimize networking, security, and cloud applications. These FPGA-based SmartNICs offload processing from CPUs, enabling ultra-fast packet capture, analysis, and security enforcement in high-speed networks. results.title: DPU SmartNIC Market Set to Disrupt Traditional Server Networking - Press Release
results.content: The growing complexity of cloud-native applications, increasing data center workloads, and the rising demand for secure, high-performance networking solutions are driving widespread adoption of**Data Processing Units (DPUs)**and**SmartNICs (Smart Network Interface Cards)**. A**DPU SmartNIC**is a programmable network interface card equipped with a Data Processing Unit capable of handling infrastructure-specific tasks independently from the host CPU. These cards offer features like**network virtualization**,**zero-trust security enforcement**,**encryption offload**,**packet filtering**, and**traffic shaping**, making them vital in hyperscale data centers and cloud computing environments. DPU SmartNICs reduce bottlenecks in network communication, enabling faster data flow between processing units and storage arraysmaking them particularly useful in high-performance computing (HPC) and AI training environments. Cloud service providers are the biggest adopters due to their scalability demands, but enterprises in finance and healthcare are investing in SmartNICs to ensure**low-latency**,**high-security**infrastructure for mission-critical applications. North America leads the global DPU SmartNIC market, driven by heavy investments in cloud computing, AI, and hyperscale infrastructure. Focused on programmable network acceleration cards for telecom and security, Napatechs SmartNICs are designed to enable**high-speed data capture**,**flow classification**, and**hardware-based analytics**.

results.title: What is a DPU in HPC and what is it used for?
results.content:
Title: What is a DPU in HPC and what is it used for?
* The DPU offloads network, security, and storage, freeing up CPU/GPU and reducing latency in HPC and cloud. **Its mission is to offload and accelerate network, security and storage functions.**, freeing the CPU for what really matters: general-purpose computing and critical applications. A data processing unit is a programmable processor, usually an SoC, that combines three pillars: **Multi-core CPU (often Arm), high-performance network interface, and hardware acceleration engines** for networking, security, storage, and analytics functions. **The DPU assumes data planes and infrastructure control** (virtualization, SDN, encryption, compression, NVMe-oF, observability, etc.), while the CPU focuses on application logic and the GPU on parallel computing. **Multi-core Arm CPU, integrated memory, high-bandwidth NIC, and dedicated accelerators** for offloads such as encryption/decryption, compression, checksum, packet processing, storage virtualization, stream introspection, and more. It offloads networking, security, and storage, and prevents CPU and GPU from waiting for data. **BlueField-3 is a full DPU that operates as a standalone node** in the PCIe route, while ConnectX-7 is a very high-performance, low-latency NIC focused on connectivity and classic offloads. BlueField-3 is not just a vitamin-enriched NIC; **It is a node with Arm+OS, accelerators, integrated PCIe switch and BMC**The BMC provides host-independent management, useful in large-scale clouds for inventory, telemetry, and secure out-of-band operations, even when the primary server is unresponsive. Comprehensive discharge produces measurable effects: **Reduced host CPU usage (e.g., with OVS and NVMe-oF), lower latency, and increased effective bandwidth**In distributed storage, moving logic to the DPU can double IOPS compared to 100% software solutions by eliminating contention and replication. Services at the DPU such as **Checksum offload, decompression, SNAP for NVMe emulation and VIRTIO-FS** They reduce copies and CPU footprints, smooth out queues, and improve sustained performance. BlueField-2 led the way and BlueField-2X incorporated an Ampere GPU, aligning the roadmap with the **AI and machine learning acceleration on the data plane itself**The acquisition of Mellanox strengthened NVIDIA's position in high-performance networking, security, and storage, integrating DOCA with CUDA and NGC into a common ecosystem. This fit has been key to the evolution of data centers from virtualization (2000s) to the cloud and, now, to **software-defined and hardware-accelerated computing**The DPU doesn't compete with x86; it distributes the work where it performs best.

Like SmartNICs, SuperNICs are SoC-based, combining advanced networking capabilities, RDMA engines, and Ethernet acceleration into a highly integrated silicon footprint. | **Deployment Target** | Basic I/O servers | Enterprise compute, mid-tier cloud | Secure edge, storage acceleration, smart clouds | Public cloud, telecom infra, AI data centers | AI/ML clusters, GPU fabrics, high-speed NICs |. | **Performance Focus** | Packet movement | Efficient networking/storage offload | Hardware offload with some programmable support | Secure, programmable infra offload | Ultra-high BW & low latency for GPUs |. results.title: Napatech Debuts 400G DPU with Altera FPGA - Converge Digest
results.content:
Title: Napatech Debuts 400G DPU with Altera FPGA - Converge Digest
Home » Napatech Debuts 400G DPU with Altera FPGA. # Napatech Debuts 400G DPU with Altera FPGA. Napatech launched its new F3070X Data Processing Unit (DPU) today, a 400G acceleration platform built on Altera’s Agilex FPGA and Intel Xeon D processor technology. The DPU targets AI, cloud, telecom, and enterprise datacenters with a design focused on ultra-low latency, flexibility, and hardware-level security. The F3070X combines FPGA programmability with CPU integration in a hardware-programmable NIC, a design intended to eliminate network bottlenecks and speed up AI pipelines, disaggregated storage, and cybersecurity tasks. Napatech will demonstrate the DPU at Altera Innovator Day in San Jose, showcasing acceleration for AI storage and backend infrastructure. Jarrod Siket, Chief Product & Marketing Officer at Napatech, said: “By partnering with Altera, we’re bringing this proven design to the next wave of cloud, enterprise, telecom, and AI datacenter operators — unlocking the same transformative benefits at every scale.”. • Napatech F3070X DPU delivers 400G acceleration using Altera Agilex FPGA and Intel Xeon D. • Live demonstrations at Altera Innovator Day include AI storage acceleration and FPGA coprocessing. 🌐 Analysis: The DPU launch marks Napatech’s move to extend FPGA-based acceleration from hyperscalers into broader markets, leveraging Altera’s common acceleration platform. Napatech A/S (OSE: NAPA.OL) is a Denmark-based company headquartered in Copenhagen that develops programmable network acceleration solutions designed to improve performance in data centers, cloud, telecom, and AI infrastructure environments. The company specializes in SmartNICs and Data Processing Units (DPUs) that leverage FPGA-based acceleration to offload and secure workloads such as networking, storage, cybersecurity, and AI pipelines. Founded in 2003, Napatech is led by CEO Henrik Brill Jensen, who has a background in telecommunications and network systems, and is supported by a management team with expertise spanning hardware, software, and FPGA design. Napatech’s technology centers on its production-grade acceleration platform, which integrates FPGA programmability with software frameworks for high-throughput, ultra-low-latency packet capture, classification, and analysis. Its core product portfolio includes programmable SmartNICs and, more recently, the F3070X DPU launched in 2025, built on Intel Altera Agilex FPGA and Xeon D processors. ### Napatech Boosts 5G UPF Offload by 60% with SmartNIC Powered by Altera’s Agilex 7. ### Napatech Unveils 400G AI SmartNIC Based on Altera FPGA.
